title: 2026-11-02_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_354
description: Investigate a compromised host infected with the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor, identify malicious activities, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malicious activities, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: To proceed to the training levels, ENTER, TYPE, or SUBMIT the passkey 'start'. You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system's IP address is `192.168.50.5`.
levels.local_content: To proceed to the training levels, ENTER, TYPE, or SUBMIT the passkey 'start'. You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, run the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for services with unusual names or descriptions. The service responsible for the suspicious activity is `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to services that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the service status and logs for any unusual activity. Use the command `journalctl -u <service_name>` to view logs.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service name is `systemkernelservicedefender.service`. This service is not part of the standard system configuration.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution: To determine the network port associated with the suspicious service, run the command `ss -tulnp` and look for ports that are not part of the standard system configuration. The network port associated with the suspicious service is `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the service configuration and network listeners. Look for ports that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all network connections and look for unusual ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious port is `80`. This port is not part of the standard system configuration.

levels.title: Suspicious Data Collection Service Discovery
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution: To identify the service responsible for collecting system information, run the command `systemctl list-timers` and look for services that collect system information and run periodically. The service responsible for collecting system information is `local-inventory.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for services that collect system information and run periodically. Check the service timers and logs.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all service timers and look for unusual services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is `local-inventory.service`. This service collects system information periodically.
